- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, creating a “peak-and-fall” pattern that doesn’t match true market behavior.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when recent history shows mean reversion.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in volatile periods.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast window (days 10–20), often failing to account for short-term volatility or policy-driven corrections.
- When true prices show a clear downward trend, model continues to project upward momentum, especially if recent history includes high values.
- Model fails to capture “reversion to mean” in cases where prices deviate significantly from historical averages, especially in the last 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model overreacts to recent spikes, producing exaggerated peaks that don’t align with actual market fundamentals or trading behavior.
